title: Easy-DHPSF 2.0: open-source software for three-dimensional localization and two-color registration of single molecules with nanoscale accuracy
protocol: Acquire raw data, calibration scan, control point scan, and dark offset images.
Save a sequence log file for calibration and control point scans.
Open an instance of the Easy-DHPSF GUI by entering ‘easy_dhpsf’ in MATLAB command line.
Set conversion gain and pixel size under ‘Setup.’
Select channel ‘G’ for green or ‘R’ for red under Setup > Channel.
Under ‘Calibrate DHPSF’, click ‘Run.’
Follow prompts to automatically save partly processed dataset after module.
Open the calibration images file.
Open the dark offset image file matching the calibration.
Open the sequence log file for the calibration.
Set the EM gain used during the acquisition of the calibration images.
Specify whether to use wavelet subtraction.
Indicate if NHA holes are present and their orientation.
Determine the DHPSF’s two lobes orientation when in focus.
Set the box radius for fitting.
Select a region of interest to analyze.
Adjust the box to select a region containing at least one bright fluorescent object.
Double-click inside the adjusted box to confirm selection.
Select an entire wide-field excitation region to estimate background fluorescence accurately.
Click the center of each DHPSF to select fluorescent objects.
Select 4 holes that form a large square.
Select fiducials to outline the edge of your field of view.
Click the center of each DHPSF, halfway between the two lobes.
Hit enter when finished with DHPSFs.
Inspect calibration information in the ‘calibration [DateAndTime]’ folder for each bead.
Ensure that the angle vs. z position curve is roughly linear.
Verify that the variation of angle measurements in each step is not unreasonably high.
Select the most reliable calibration bead using the drop-down menu in the Easy-DHPSF main window.
Use the calibration information and templates generated from this bead for all later processing steps.
Repeat the calibration process for the other color channel.
Under Setup > Channel, select a channel ‘G’ for green or ‘R’ for red.
Click the ‘Run’ button in the ‘Calibrate SM identification’ panel.
Load in the dark offset .tif file with the same parameters as the SM data.
Choose a background processing algorithm such as median filtering, wavelet filtering, or no background subtraction.
Select a region containing the SMs of interest for analysis.
Open the ’threshold [DateAndTime]’ folder after completing the template-matching module.
Select appropriate thresholds for each template.
Enter these thresholds into the ‘threshold’ field in the GUI.
Click the ‘Run’ button in the ‘Track fiduciaries’ panel.
Follow prompts to automatically save the GUI if desired.
Select a region of interest containing at least one bright fiducial by adjusting the box and double-clicking inside it.
Select one or more fiducials by clicking in the center of each DHPSF.
Click the ‘Run’ button in the ‘Localize DHPSF SMs’ panel.
Follow the prompts if you would like to automatically save the GUI after this module.
Choose the frames from the raw data to process, as well as whether you would like to estimate the laser profile and find true lobe widths (sigmas).
Monitor the analysis process to ensure that the threshold includes single molecules visible in the raw data.
Ensure that fits are performed successfully.
Save the Easy-DHPSF file using the save icon at the top of the GUI, ensuring the correct Channel is selected.
Go back to Step 2 and select the other color channel.
Ensure you have two saved easy-dhpsf files, one for each color.
Load in the Easy-DHPSF GUI file from Step 1, saved after calibrating both green and red channels.
Select a channel ‘G’ for green or ‘R’ for red under Setup > Channel.
Click ‘Run’ in the ‘Calibrate SM identification’ panel.
Follow the prompts to automatically save the GUI after this module if desired.
Set the EM Gain used, load control point scan .tif file(s), and select frames for control point detection calibration.
Ensure selected frames include at least 1-2 full axial scans across different z positions.
Load in the sequence log file (.dat or .mat) with the sequence of steps used for the control point scan.
Load in dark offset .tif with the same parameters as the control point scan.
Select background median filtering or wavelet filtering.
Fill in median filtering parameters if chosen.
Select NHA if using a Nano-Localization Array (NHA).
Perform median background subtraction if NHA is selected.
Prompt the user to select an ROI of the correct color channel using a square ROI.
Allow the user to select an ROI with a polygon.
Follow Steps 2.4-2.5 for selecting thresholds after calibration.
Click the ‘Run’ button in the ‘Localize DHPSF SMs’ panel.
Choose frames you would like to fit.
Estimate laser profile and find true lobe sigmas if desired.
Enter the number of stationary frames for each axial position and click ‘OK.’
If using an NHA, select 4 fiducials that form a box outlining the field of view.
Once the program finishes fitting, filter and export your results by clicking ‘Filter Output’ under ‘Output DHPSF SM localization.’
If using a NHA, choose ‘Yes’ to use spatially dependent calibrations when prompted.
A different calibration may be used during this step if prompted by the program.
Filter control points as prompted by the program.
Choose the region to be plotted in the scatter plot.
Inspect localizations and save data when satisfied with results.
Repeat steps for the other color channel.
Run the MATLAB function ‘Identify_ControlPoints_3D_v1.m’.
Open the ‘Output.mat’ data file with molecule fits in the GREEN channel.
Open the ‘Output.mat’ data file with the molecule fits in transmitted/RED channel.
Open the .mat or .dat sequence log file for the control point scan.
If available, open a previous transform to use as an initial guess. Otherwise, click ‘Cancel’

Input parameters of how many stationary frames were taken at each z position, how many frames to wait before starting the averaging, and if using an old transform, how closely the initial transform should match old transform points.
The program will first find control point (CP) candidates, merging localizations at given z positions.
A figure will pop up with fitting statistics for the molecules fits you loaded. Enter filtering parameters for σx, σy, σz, and number of measurements.
Inspect averaged bead positions in both channels.
Hand click at least 15 control points if an initial transform was not given.
Follow prompts to select control points until the program stops asking for more or you hit ‘esc’ after selecting over 15 control points.
The program will generate a preliminary transformation file located in the same directory as your green channel ‘Output.mat’.
Evaluate the initial transform calculated from control points.
Generate a final 3D transform using the evaluated initial transform.
Run the MATLAB function 'EvaluateTransform_3D_v2.m'.
Input transformation parameters or click to evaluate parameter ranges.
Enter the range of parameters for evaluation.
The program will return target registration errors (TRE) and fiducial registration errors (FRE).
Select the value of nearest neighbors, sigma, and kth nearest neighbor.
Input these parameters into the dialog box.
The program calculates a transformation using provided parameters.
The program returns a histogram of TREs and FREs.
The final transformation is '3D_Transform_lwquadratic'.
Run the MATLAB script 'TransformSMACMData_v6.m'.
Indicate whether the green data or red data was acquired first, or if the two-color acquisition was interleaved.
Load the green Easy-DHPSF file and perform smoothing via wavelet filtering of the fiducial tracks.
Apply the smoothing correction to the green data following the prompts that appear.
Load the red Easy-DHPSF file and follow prompts to smooth the fiducial track data for the red channel.
Load in the '3D_Transform_lwquadratic.mat' file generated in a previous step.
Prompt whether or not to crop each dataset before transformation.
Select the location and enter a file name for where to save your registered dataset.
Store the registered data in the MATLAB structure ‘dataSets,’ with ‘dataSets(1)’ containing the green data and ‘dataSets(2)’ containing the red data.
Select whether you would like to export the localizations into a csv file.
Choose the location and file name of each color file if exporting.
